newsitem.title: CANADA: Brascan shrs rise on Edper merger.
newsitem.headline: Brascan shrs rise on Edper merger.

text.p: Shares in Brascan Ltd rose in hectic early trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Wednesday after the conglomerate said it would merge with Edper Group Ltd to simplify the group's corporate structure.
Analysts said the merger proposal, announced on Tuesday, left Brascan shares undervalued at their Tuesday halt price price of 30.75.
Under the plan, holders of Brascan class A shares will receive 1.5 class A limited voting shares of the new company, to be called Edper Brascan Corp, for each Brascan share held.
Edper shares were halted at 23.05 on Tuesday.
Both stocks resumed trading on Wednesday.

Brascan rose 3.25 to 34 in Toronto before backing off to trade up 3 at 33.75 on turnover of more than 1.3 million shares. The shares were up 2-3/8 to 24-1/4 in light trade on the American Stock Exchange.

"The key is whether the Edper Group goes down, and it hasn't. If the Edper Group doesn't go down, then I'm going to be getting stock that's worth 34.50. So Brascan at 30.75 would be undervalued and it would logically go up. And that's what is has done," said TD Securities Inc analyst Terrence Fisher.
Edper shares slipped 0.10 to 22.95 on the TSE in moderate trade.
Fisher said Edper stock would likely hold steady in the face of the merger.
"I think it's a good deal. There don't seem to be any negatives, really...it's not materially dilutive to the Edper shareholders, so why would it go down?" Fisher said.
Brascan reported first-quarter earnings of C$0.49 a share on Wednesday, up from C$0.48 from a year earlier.
Analysts said the earnings were in line with expectations. Brascan has stakes in several companies, including Noranda Inc, Trilon Financial Corp and Great Lakes Power Inc.
"I don't think that's going to surprise anybody. If anything, it might be a little bit on the plus side. Noranda did not have a big quarter," one analyst said.
